question: Can a first-order policy gradient method reach the data efficiency and reliability of TRPO while allowing multiple epochs of minibatch updates on each batch of sampled data?
hypothesis: A surrogate objective with clipped probability ratios gives a pessimistic (lower-bound) estimate of policy performance that keeps updates small enough to run several optimisation epochs per batch stably.
contributions: A family of policy gradient methods (PPO) alternating between sampling and optimising a surrogate objective for multiple epochs of minibatch SGD
A clipped probability-ratio surrogate objective L^CLIP, plus an adaptive KL-penalty variant
Comparison of surrogate variants on 7 MuJoCo tasks, and of PPO against TRPO, CEM, vanilla PG, A2C, A2C+trust region, ACER on continuous control and Atari

method.summary: PPO collects T timesteps from each of N parallel actors with the old policy, computes truncated GAE advantages, then optimises a clipped surrogate (optionally combined with value loss and entropy bonus) with minibatch SGD/Adam for K epochs. Variants with no clipping, fixed KL penalty and adaptive KL penalty are compared on 7 MuJoCo tasks; clipped PPO is then compared with other algorithms on MuJoCo, Roboschool humanoids and 49 Atari games.
method.task: Deep reinforcement learning policy optimisation (continuous control and Atari)

datasets.name: OpenAI Gym MuJoCo -v1 (HalfCheetah, Hopper, InvertedDoublePendulum, InvertedPendulum, Reacher, Swimmer, Walker2d)
datasets.split: 3 random seeds per task per setting

datasets.name: Roboschool humanoid tasks (Humanoid-v0, HumanoidFlagrun-v0, HumanoidFlagrunHarder-v0)
datasets.size: up to 50M (Humanoid) / 100M (Flagrun tasks) timesteps, read from Fig 4 axes

datasets.name: Arcade Learning Environment (49 Atari games in OpenAI Gym)

models.name: PPO MuJoCo policy
models.architecture: fully-connected MLP, two hidden layers of 64 units, tanh, outputs mean of a Gaussian with variable standard deviations; separate value function (no parameter sharing)

models.name: PPO Atari policy
models.architecture: same policy network architecture as Mnih et al. 2016 (A2C)

models.name: TRPO, CEM, vanilla PG (adaptive stepsize), A2C, A2C+trust region, ACER

other.tuning: tuned implementations; Atari baseline hyperparameters tuned to maximise performance on the benchmark (values not given)

training.objective: L^CLIP+VF+S = E_t[L^CLIP - c1 L^VF + c2 S[pi_theta](s_t)], with L^CLIP = E_t[min(r_t A_t, clip(r_t, 1-eps, 1+eps) A_t)], eps e.g. 0.2; L^VF = (V_theta(s_t) - V_targ_t)^2; advantages by truncated GAE
training.optimizer: Adam (minibatch SGD in the algorithm statement)
training.lr: MuJoCo: 3e-4 (Adam stepsize); Atari: 2.5e-4 x alpha; Roboschool: adjusted from KL target (no value)
training.lr_schedule: Atari: alpha linearly annealed from 1 to 0 over learning (also scales epsilon = 0.1 x alpha); Roboschool log stdev of action distribution LinearAnneal(-0.7, -1.6)
training.batch_size: minibatch M <= NT; MuJoCo 64; Roboschool 4096; Atari 32 x 8
training.steps: MuJoCo 1M timesteps; Atari 40M frames (10M timesteps); Roboschool up to 100M timesteps (read from Fig 4)
training.epochs: K epochs per batch: MuJoCo 10, Roboschool 15, Atari 3
training.regularisation: entropy bonus c2 = 0.01 (Atari only); clipping eps; optional KL penalty
training.seeds: 3 random seeds per environment (MuJoCo and Atari)

other.adaptive_kl: if d < dtarg/1.5 then beta <- beta/2; if d > dtarg x 1.5 then beta <- beta x 2; beta initialised at 1 in Table 1 experiments; factors 1.5 and 2 chosen heuristically
other.hyperparameter_search: epsilon and KL (beta, dtarg) searched over in Sec 6.1; search procedure not described

inference.samples: 3 seeds per env; Table 1 averages 21 runs (7 envs x 3 seeds)

metrics.name: avg. normalized score (MuJoCo)
metrics.definition: per run, average total reward of last 100 episodes; per environment scores shifted and scaled so random policy = 0 and best result = 1; averaged over 21 runs

metrics.name: Atari avg episode reward over all of training
metrics.definition: average reward per episode over the entire training period (favours fast learning)

metrics.name: Atari avg episode reward over last 100 episodes
metrics.definition: average reward per episode over last 100 episodes of training (favours final performance)

metrics.name: games won
metrics.definition: number of games in which an algorithm has the best metric, averaged across three trials

baselines: Vanilla policy gradient with adaptive stepsize
eval.protocol: 3 seeds per environment; no significance test stated

limits: Clipping epsilon and KL settings were searched on only 7 MuJoCo tasks with 3 seeds each at 1M timesteps.
No significance tests; baselines are 'tuned' but their hyperparameters are not given.
On final Atari performance ACER wins more games (28 vs 19); PPO's edge is sample efficiency (fast learning).
Claims of better wall-time, simplicity and robustness are stated without timing or compute figures.
Hardware, compute, wall-clock and number of actors for MuJoCo are not stated.
Multiple-epoch updates on plain L^PG are said to cause destructively large updates, but those results are not shown.
